Everyone knows they’re supposed to brush twice a day… but no one really teaches you HOW to brush. 🪥🦷 Brushing isn’t about scrubbing harder. It’s all about technique. ✨ Use a soft-bristled toothbrush. ✨ Angle the bristles at 45 degrees toward the gumline. ✨ Use gentle, circular motions along the gingival margin where plaque loves to hide. ✨ Brush for 2 full minutes. ✨ And don’t forget your tongue! Your tongue can harbor bacteria that contribute to bad breath. But bad breath can also be caused by plaque buildup, cavities, tartar accumulation, dry mouth, and sometimes even issues related to the digestive system. The goal isn’t to “scrub your teeth clean.” In fact, brushing too hard can lead to gum recession and wear away tooth structure over time. Gentle. Thorough. Consistent. Sometimes it’s not that people aren’t brushing… it’s that no one ever showed them the proper technique. 💙 #oralhealtips #sdh #dentalhygienist #howto #teethtok

📚Build a Study Schedule That Actually Works 1. Count the weeks until your exam, then divide your syllabus across those weeks. Know your pace. 2. Build buffer weeks into your schedule — life happens. Flexible plans survive, rigid ones collapse. 3. Assign subjects to specific days: don't try to cover all subjects daily. Batch by subject for depth. 4. Schedule review sessions BEFORE new content — start each week by reviewing the previous week first. 5. Your peak energy hours should be reserved for hardest subjects. Schedule light review for low-energy times. 6. Review your study schedule every Sunday. What worked? What didn't? Adjust and move forward. #StudyTok #StudyMotivation #ExamPrep #StudyHacks #StudyWithMe

📚Remember Anything With These Tricks 1. Mnemonics: create an acronym or silly phrase using the first letters of a list you need to memorize. 2. The Memory Palace: visualize walking through your house and 'placing' facts in specific rooms. 3. Rhymes and songs make information sticky — set boring content to a tune and it becomes unforgettable. 4. Association: link new information to something you already know well. New knowledge needs an anchor. 5. Repetition with variation: say it, write it, draw it, teach it. Four formats = four times the retention. 6. The weirder your memory trick, the more effective it is. Bizarre associations are impossible to forget. #StudyTok #StudyMotivation #ExamPrep #StudyHacks #StudyWithMe

“Dog lovers” vs dog lovers when it comes to greeting dogs! ETA: “dog lovers” could also be replaced with “uniformed, uneducated, and/or inconsiderate dog lovers” vs “informed, educated, and considerate dog lovers” if that makes you more comfortable 🫶 One of my biggest pet peeves is people baby talking to my dog and pretending like I’m interrupting? Bizarre! And in case you didn’t know because it’s something that’s been so normalized, putting your hands in dogs’ faces is unsafe. Dogs don’t need to sniff you up close like that and it’s putting unneeded pressure on them (often leading to bites). The best way to greet a dog is calm, neutral, and honestly just ignoring them. If you want to say hi to a dog, ask the owner first. Try to make yourself small by turning to the side and crouching. Allow the dog to approach you first. Some dogs are super friendly and love people! This doesn’t mean it’s ok to pet or approach without asking their handler! The safest way to greet any dog is by admiring from afar. Admittedly, if I know someone’s dog well, I might be a bit of the former “dog lover” and be excitedly greeting them 😂 It’s different when you know the dog! Dumbbell Sumo Squat  Know the difference  1. Dumbbell Position Hold the dumbbell with both hands naturally hanging between your legs, rather than holding it at your chest. This allows you to lift heavier weights without being limited by arm strength. 2. Torso Posture Maintain a slight forward lean instead of staying fully upright. Leaning forward increases hip flexion, helping to stretch and better activate the glutes. 3. Stance Width and Foot Angle Set your feet about 1.5 times shoulder-width apart, with your toes pointing outward at roughly a 45-degree angle. If the stance is too wide, the inner thigh muscles (adductors) will take over, reducing glute activation. 4. Load Path As you squat down, the dumbbell should not stay directly under your shoulders. Instead, it should fall slightly behind the midline, closer to your posterior chain. Bring your hands slightly inward to keep the load closer to your center of mass, which helps reduce lower back strain and improves movement efficiency. #gymtips #quads #gluteworkout #gym #gymrat
